title: How to Choose the Right eBike: Class, Motor, Range & Fit
author: Quest Watersports
summary_html: Class, motor, battery range, frame style and tires: a practical guide to picking the right eBike, plus why a test ride matters.
body_html:
Shopping for an eBike should be exciting, not confusing. Classes, motors, batteries and frame styles all affect how a bike feels. This guide breaks down the choices in plain language, so you can walk into a test ride knowing what to look for.

Start with how you will ride

Before comparing specs, answer three questions:

  • Where? Crushed limestone trails like the I&M Canal, neighborhood streets, a commute or hilly singletrack?
  • How far? A 10-mile loop or a full day?
  • Who? Do you need a bike that fits a different rider height, or one that carries cargo?

Step 1: Understand the class

Illinois recognizes three classes of low-speed eBike, each with a 750-watt or smaller motor:

  • Class 1: pedal assist up to 20 mph. Easy to ride and widely accepted on trails.
  • Class 2: a throttle plus pedal assist, up to 20 mph. Good if you want a break from pedaling.
  • Class 3: pedal assist up to 28 mph. Faster, with tighter age and access rules.

Class affects where and by whom a bike may be ridden. Read our Illinois eBike laws guide before you decide.

Step 2: Choose a motor type

Hub motors

The motor sits in the rear wheel. Hub motors are simple, affordable and a good fit for most recreational and commuting riders. Several Aventon bikes we carry, such as the Aventure and Level REC, use 750W hub motors.

Mid-drive motors

The motor sits at the pedals and drives the chain. That delivers natural-feeling power, more torque on climbs and better weight balance. Mid-drive bikes tend to cost more. Aventon's Level 4 ADV, Aventure M and Ramblas ADV are examples.

Step 3: Think about battery range

Manufacturers publish a maximum range, but your result will be different. Real range depends on:

  • How high you set the assist level.
  • Throttle use. It drains the battery faster.
  • Rider and cargo weight.
  • Wind, hills and temperature.
  • Tire pressure and surface.

Treat published range as a ceiling. Our rental Aventon Pace bikes are rated up to 40 miles per charge, which is plenty for most of the I&M Canal Trail. If you want a long ride without stopping, shop for a larger battery. Otherwise plan stops on the Quest eBike Charging Network.

Step 4: Pick a frame style

  • Step-over: the traditional bike frame. Stiffer and often a bit lighter.
  • Step-through: a low frame that is easy to mount and dismount. It's popular with riders of every age, and great if you carry gear or have limited flexibility.

Many of our Aventon models, such as the Aventure and Sinch, come in both styles. Frame size matters as much as style, so ask us to check your fit.

Step 5: Decide on tire width

Standard tires

Lighter, faster and efficient on pavement and packed trails. Ideal for commuting and crushed limestone.

Fat tires

Fat tires, such as the 4-inch puncture-resistant tires on Aventon's Aventure line, give you traction on sand, gravel, snow and rough ground. They add weight and rolling resistance but make the ride comfortable and confident.

Step 6: Other features that matter

  • Suspension: a front fork or seatpost suspension smooths bumps. Full suspension is for serious trail riding.
  • Brakes: look for hydraulic or strong disc brakes, since eBikes are heavier.
  • Racks and fenders: some models include them. They make commuting easier.
  • Cargo capacity: the Aventon Abound is a long-tail cargo model designed to carry more weight.
  • Lights and display: you can add lights and accessories later.

Browse bike parts and accessories for lights, racks, bags, pumps and other add-ons.

What kinds of bikes do we carry?

Quest Watersports is an Aventon dealer. The lineup includes trail and mountain bikes, fat tire bikes, commuter and recreation bikes and cargo models. Stock and special orders change, so check the eBikes collection or our eBike page, then call to confirm sizes and colors.

Test ride first

A spec sheet can't tell you how a bike feels. When you test ride, pay attention to:

  • Standing height and reach. Can you put a foot down comfortably?
  • How smoothly the assist kicks in.
  • Braking and handling at slow speeds.
  • Weight when you lift or walk the bike.
  • Comfort of the saddle, grips and posture.

If you aren't sure, rent first. Our eBike rentals let you spend a few hours on the trail before you buy.

Assembly and tuning

An eBike should be put together and adjusted properly. Many of our bikes are subject to an assembly and tuning fee, which covers building and tuning the bike so it's safe, shifting well and ready to ride. Ask which fee applies to the model you choose. After the sale, our team can help with service questions and parts.

Register for warranty

If you buy an Aventon, register your bike with the manufacturer for warranty coverage using the link on our eBike page.

Visit us for a test ride

Stop by 1851 Old Chicago Rd, Ottawa, IL 61350, Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, or call 815.433.2200 to ask about a model, size or color.

FAQ

Which eBike class should I buy?

Class 1 is the simplest and most widely accepted choice. Choose Class 2 if you want a throttle, and Class 3 only if you want higher assisted speed and understand the extra age and access rules.

Hub motor or mid-drive?

Hub motors are simple and affordable. Mid-drive motors cost more but offer natural-feeling power and better climbing.

How far will an eBike go on one charge?

Published range is a maximum. Real range depends on assist level, throttle use, weight, wind and terrain. Our rental eBikes are rated for up to 40 miles per charge.

Do I need a fat tire eBike?

Only if you ride on sand, loose gravel or rough ground. Standard tires work well for pavement and crushed limestone trails.

Can I test ride before buying?

Yes. Stop in during sales hours or call us. You can also rent an eBike at Heritage Harbor before you buy.

Does Quest assemble the bike?

Yes. Many bikes carry an assembly and tuning fee covering build and setup. Ask which applies to your model.
